title: Suarez’s three modes of adoration toward an image: exemplar alone; exemplar+image as one; image alone for the exemplar’s sake
source_text: V. Caeterum quanquam tota Ecclesia & Schola Romana in eo consentiat, Imaginibus Christi & Sanctorum cultum aliquem exhiberi & posse & debere, eumque cultum recte & convenienter adorationis voce significari; pluribus tamen ostensum est in cultus illius natura explicanda, multum inter se discrepare Scholae Romanae Doctores, ac super eo in varias abire sententias. Quae varietas ut melius capi possit & breviter ob oculos poni, advertendum est cum Francisco Suarez tribus modis intelligi posse fieri adorationem ad imaginem, seu in praesentia imaginis. Primo dirigendo totam mentis intentionem ad exemplar in imagine repraesentatum, tanquam ad objectum proprie, per se, & corde adoratum, & non ad imaginem. Secundo dirigendo adorationem tam ad exemplar repraesentatum, quam ad imaginem in qua repraesentatur, ex utroque, mente & animo conficiendo unum objectum adaequatum, ad quod per se terminatur, & quod sit adaequata materia circa quam versetur adoratio, ex intentione adorantis. Tertio, dirigendo adorationem ad solam imaginem, tanquam ad materiam, seu rem per se adoratam, ad exemplar vero solum, ut ad rationem adorandi. Tomo primo in tertiam Thomae disput. 54. Sect. 4.
pass_a_gloss: But although the whole Roman Church and School agree in this, that some cult both can and ought to be exhibited to the Images of Christ and of the Saints, and that that cult is rightly and fittingly signified by the word adoration; yet it has been shown in many ways that in explaining the nature of that cult the Doctors of the Roman School differ much among themselves, and go off into various opinions upon it. Which variety, that it may be better grasped and briefly set before the eyes, it is to be noted with Francis Suarez that adoration toward an image, or in the presence of an image, can be understood to be done in three modes. First, by directing the whole intention of the mind to the exemplar represented in the image, as to the object properly, per se, and in the heart adored, and not to the image. Second, by directing adoration both to the exemplar represented and to the image in which it is represented, composing from both, with mind and soul, one adequate object, to which it is terminated per se, and which is the adequate matter about which the adoration turns, from the intention of the adorer. Third, by directing adoration to the image alone, as to the matter, or thing adored per se, but to the exemplar alone as to the reason of adoring. In the first volume on the third of Thomas, disputation 54, section 4.
pass_b_english: Rome agrees images get some adoratio, yet Schoolmen split on how.
Suarez lists three modes: mind wholly on the exemplar; exemplar and image as one adequate object; image alone as matter, exemplar as reason.
Thomas III, disp. 54.4 is his locus.

choices.why: Named sorter of the three modes.
